title: Add records-history cutover with import and catch-up at C0
summary: Add [history] cutover_job; on landing that job (and via a catch-up in the reconcile step of land and status, idempotent), run the importer at C0 and write the legacy-exempt record. The history check judges commits up to C0 by old rules and later ones by attribution, unchanged before C0 exists; CI keeps its name and fetches athena/records first.

defaults_applied.how: All changes and tests in Rust.
New tests for land, catch-up, history; cargo test and clippy clean.
Criteria run tests exercising the behavior.
Decisions and changelog written for outside readers.
CI and config enforce the cutover.
Catch-up test asserts the import actually wrote commits, not just an empty no-op.
One focused change over the listed files.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: make the records-history cutover work so maintainers and CI judge history by records after C0; audience is the Athena maintainer and the verifier.
The job's own id is taken from the job context (the landing job id); cutover_job is set to it in athena.toml.
The existing importer in records_import.rs and the attribution check in attribution.rs are reused; only wiring and idempotence markers are added.
Idempotence is detected by presence of an import commit/manifest on athena/records.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: a scratch-repository test lands the job named by [history] cutover_job via the land path and shows the records branch has the landing record, an import commit with import-manifest.json whose self-check passes, and the legacy-exempt record (six exempt entries plus 02837e0, each with a reason), with C0 resolved from the landing record's host commit.

Run `cargo test`: a catch-up test shows that when the cutover job has a landing record on athena/records but no import commit, the reconcile step at the start of land and status runs the import at C0 and writes the legacy-exempt record; a second reconcile writes nothing (idempotent).

Run `cargo test`: a history test shows a commit at or before C0 judged by the old trailer rules and a commit after C0 judged only by the attribution check against records, so a later records-only commit with no trailer passes.
Run `cargo test`: with no cutover_job set, or before its landing record exists on the records branch, all pre-existing history-check tests pass with their expectations unedited.

athena.toml [history] sets cutover_job to this job's own id; crates/athena-data/src/config.rs parses it as optional; .github/workflows/ci.yml keeps the job name 'the full history' and fetches athena/records before the history check.
docs/decisions.md records the cutover design (C0 definition, import at C0, legacy-exempt record, catch-up reconcile, behavior before C0, trailers still written) and CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean; `cargo test` passes overall.

departures: Larger than reference: multi-crate change plus a catch-up path and scratch-repo tests.
